lines.speaker: rook
lines.text: Well. The one who walked up from the Low Ford at dawn. Chid came in babbling about blue lights going out at the crossing, and here you are, bleeding on my step. I'm Rook. This is the Last Lamp. Sit down before you fall down.

answers: Can you keep some things for me?
That lamp over the door. It's from the Chapel of the Morning Light.
There's a grave in the garden behind the shrine. A captain, with his lamp.
Who else has come up the Low Ford road?

direction.pace: brisk, dry, bossy at the end
direction.wants: to get the stranger sat down and fed
direction.notes: She already knows who you are (she's paid to know; Vonnra's money is under the 'Well.'). Chid's babbling is a fond eye-roll. 'Sit down before you fall down' is kindness as an order: warm and bossy, no softening.

lines.speaker: rook
lines.text: Another one off the Low Ford road. I'm Rook, and this is the Last Lamp: bed, bread, a bath if you ask nicely, and a strongroom for what you'd rather not carry about.

answers: Can you keep some things for me?
That lamp over the door. It's from the Chapel of the Morning Light.

direction.wants: to sell a bed and size up a guest
direction.notes: 'Another one off the Low Ford road' is a note she'll pass to Vonnra later, said lightly. The services rattle off like a counted list; 'if you ask nicely' with a dry twinkle.

lines.text: The water's clean and the wolves are back in the deep wood. I was wrong about them. Don't tell anyone I said so.

Maeca's right more often than I'd like. She's earned that. ...She's earned a lot of things she never got.
Boots, for a start. I counted boots for the Ashford garrison, once, and I was good at it. That's all you're getting. Something else?
That's his fang. That's the old devil himself. Fifty, as promised, and my thanks with it.
That's his fang. That's the old devil himself. Fifty, as promised, and my thanks with it.
Coyle's wagons never reached my gate. The Old Road was open all day; I had men on it dawn to dusk. Whatever happened to them happened off the road, and whoever told them otherwise lied.
Somebody who knew they were coming, what they carried and which clerk could be bought. That's a short list in a town this size, and I don't like a single name on it.
Sick or bold, they bite the same. ...But if you're right, and you can show me what's sickening them, I'd rather fix the cause than pay for pelts till I'm old.
The lamplings. Of course it's the lamplings. Then I'm done paying for pelts: I'll not pay men to put down sick dogs. Deal with the pump. I'll keep watching the road.
You sold the Coyle cargo to a fence. Everyone in the Waystation knows it, and so do I. A hundred gold to the Watch and we'll say no more about it. Or you can leave my town.
I hear you put the old grey one down. I'd stopped paying for it. You did it anyway. I'm trying to work out what that makes you.
The Roost burned with the cages full. I've hanged men for less. I can't prove you lit it, and you know I can't, and I'd like you to know that I know that.
Three teamsters walked in through my gate, thin as rakes and alive. You did what eleven Watchmen couldn't. Don't let it go to your head; eleven Watchmen can't do much.
Somebody told Redcowl the Watch was coming, and he ran. The Watch was in bed. ...I'd ask you not to use my name in vain. But it worked. Did it work? It worked.
Course it is. Keep it to yourself. I've enough to count.
Heard you went back for whatever killed you and took your things off it. I've known men who wouldn't go back for their own boots.

Mine. From the north, about the north. (The cup doesn't move.) Read your own post, if anybody writes to you.

before.said: The animals were never like this. Never. And the water's tasted wrong all year: metal, and smoke. Bring me some from the Thornhollow stream, above the blight if you can, below it if you must, and I'l…

Tam. Course Tam saw it; nobody watches the ground like a boy with nothing to do. Drank and fell down. Not fought, not starved: drank. ...Bring me that water. A bottle, from where he saw them. I've be…

Green water, and— what's this? From a pipe? Ember. Ember slurry: the dust of the stones, cooked and watered down. Rots the belly of anything that drinks it. And nobody spills this much by accident. S…

You know your salts. Yes, precipitate it, there, and— ember. Slurry, and fresh. Look at the grain: it's been through a pump. Nobody pumps ember but the lamplings, and the lamplings answer to Grimtunn…

Who digs? Who burns ember by the barrow-load? The lamplings. Find where it goes into the water and you'll find their pipe. Take an antidote or two, and don't drink anything out there. Not even if it'…

There. Go on, then, and be warm.

The Order made it, I think. Before the Watch. Before me, certainly, which is a long time. Everything the Morning Light made was made to guard something. That's the trouble with guards: they outlast w…
The old empire did something there, before the Watch. I think the Watch was founded to keep it done. I don't know what. Vonnra does. Vonnra won't say. That, I think, is the answer.
Digging. Down. The Order used to say the dark's only light that hasn't been found yet. I never liked that one. It sounds like a threat.
Oh, ages. Since— well. Rook's mother used to bring me bread. Lovely woman. Terrible bread. ...Is that the time? I should light a candle.
You went through the door! You went through— what was on the stair? No, don't tell me. Yes, tell me. No.
Then they're still keeping it. Good. Good, I think. ...I'm going to light every candle I've got.
The Warden's heart. Rook says a lampling took it at the ford. ...Oh, dear. Oh, dear, dear. That was one of the old ones. They're not meant to be carried about.
You got your things back! From the thing! Was it horrible? It was horrible. Sit down. Not there. There.
A shield! The Order's knights carried shields with the morning painted on them. Yours has... dents. Dents are good. Dents mean it worked.

Can I ask you something? Your mother's name. ...No, don't tell me. You had to think. I saw you think. Write the names down, somewhere you'll find them. It always takes the names first. Then the faces…
Loud! Everybody thinks priests are quiet. We sang at breakfast. Brother Aumery could sing bread warm. ...They're all gone now. I keep thinking I'll get used to that. I keep not.

Was there! (He's suddenly very interested in a candle.) A C. Lovely. Lots of people start with C. Cuthbert. Cressida. There was a Cormac, once, who— (He stops.) It's a lovely old hand, whoever it was…

We buried Nell behind the shrine, next to old Ashe. Brannoc made the marker himself. Iron. Of course, iron. (He is quiet, which he never is.) She was very light. ...Sit down a minute. Not there. Ther…

before.said: I see an old wolf who let you into his house, and you, coming back to it with his children's blood on your hands. Whatever else you did about the wolves, he will remember that first. So will I.

direction.wants: to remind them the work is unfinished
direction.notes: 'Neither are you' has a double weight she alone understands: she has plans for them. Keep it level.

lines.speaker: vonnra
lines.text: And Pell Varrow, in a cage that was built for someone else. You know which one. He is still counting. It is all he has left to do.

before.said: And six crates in a bandit's tent, guarded now by a man who knows what they are for. He will not sell them. He is saving them. I wonder for what.

direction.wants: to let them see a schemer caught in his own trap
direction.notes: 'Built for someone else' carries the cut. 'It is all he has left to do' has a sliver of pity, the kind one keeper of accounts feels for another.

lines.speaker: vonnra
lines.text: And Pell. Pell in irons, being walked to the cells, telling everyone who will listen that he has friends. He does. They are not in this town.

before.said: And six crates in a bandit's tent, guarded now by a man who knows what they are for. He will not sell them. He is saving them. I wonder for what.

direction.pace: slow, a measured beat before 'They are not in this town'
direction.wants: to hint at the reach of Pell's connections
direction.notes: The repeated 'Pell' is faintly mocking. The last sentence is a warning lightly dressed as gossip.

lines.speaker: vonnra
lines.text: And a ledger, with your name in it, in Pell's small tidy hand. You were paid. So was everyone else in that book. I would keep an eye on all of them.

before.said: And six crates in a bandit's tent, guarded now by a man who knows what they are for. He will not sell them. He is saving them. I wonder for what.

direction.wants: to remind them they are now in someone's books
direction.notes: She knows what it is to have names in a ledger; she has bought plenty. 'I would keep an eye on all of them' is genuine advice, and includes herself.

lines.speaker: vonnra
lines.text: And an empty warehouse, and a man on a fast horse who will not stop until he is somewhere that has never heard of the Coyle Company. He will not forget you.

before.said: And six crates in a bandit's tent, guarded now by a man who knows what they are for. He will not sell them. He is saving them. I wonder for what.

direction.pace: slow, a long rolling sentence then a short one
direction.wants: to warn them of a grudge travelling south
direction.notes: The fast horse is said with the stillness of someone who never runs. Last line flat and certain, not dramatic.

lines.speaker: vonnra
lines.text: And Pell Varrow, counting. He is always counting. One day he will count you.

before.said: And six crates in a bandit's tent, guarded now by a man who knows what they are for. He will not sell them. He is saving them. I wonder for what.

direction.pace: slow, the last sentence slower still
direction.wants: to warn them they are on someone's tally
direction.notes: Two counters regarding each other. 'One day he will count you' is gentle and chilling; she is counting them already.

lines.speaker: vonnra
lines.text: And you. You have already died on this road. Most people only get to do that the once. Something did not want you to stay down, and I would very much like to know what.

before.said: And Pell Varrow, in a cage that was built for someone else. You know which one. He is still counting. It is all he has left to do.

direction.pace: very slow, long pause before 'and I would very much'
direction.wants: to watch their face while pretending not to know
direction.notes: She knows exactly what did not want them to stay down: she did. Say 'I would very much like to know what' with perfect, mild sincerity; the lie must be invisible.

lines.speaker: vonnra
lines.text: And you. The Watch has your description. It is not flattering.

before.said: And Pell Varrow, in a cage that was built for someone else. You know which one. He is still counting. It is all he has left to do.

direction.pace: slow, a beat before the last sentence
direction.wants: to puncture their standing
direction.notes: Her one near-joke. Bone-dry; no smile in the voice, only in the word 'flattering'.

lines.speaker: vonnra
lines.text: And you, who smell of the Pack now. Dogs in the square will not bark at you. People will.

before.said: And Pell Varrow, in a cage that was built for someone else. You know which one. He is still counting. It is all he has left to do.

direction.wants: to tell them what the town now thinks of them
direction.notes: The contrast between dogs and people is quietly pointed. A small, cool pleasure in the phrasing.

lines.speaker: vonnra
lines.text: And you. You came up the Low Ford road at night, and the lamps lit for you. They have not done that for anyone in a long time.

before.said: And Pell Varrow, in a cage that was built for someone else. You know which one. He is still counting. It is all he has left to do.

direction.pace: very slow, long pause after 'lit for you'
direction.wants: to admire her work without claiming it
direction.notes: She lit those lamps herself. 'They have not done that for anyone in a long time' carries a hush close to tenderness; she must not sound like she is confessing.

lines.speaker: vonnra
lines.text: Last. Under the Verge, something is turning over in its sleep, and under a farm past the Old Road, something is knocking to be let in. The little lamp-people are digging down to it with the Warden's heart in their arms, and they think it will be grateful. And the door in the hillside...

direction.wants: to show them the shape of what is coming
direction.notes: The fullest picture she gives; she knows it all from lore and reports. Contempt-tinged pity for the lamp-people on 'grateful'. Trail off on 'the door in the hillside...' and leave it hanging.

direction.notes: As the longer reading, without the farm. Weight on 'grateful', with a sliver of pity; leave the door hanging unfinished.

lines.speaker: vonnra

before.said: You opened it. ...Do not sit, traveller. I would rather you stood. What did you see on the stair?

lines.speaker: vonnra

lines.speaker: vonnra

lines.text: Old-empire. Square. My grandmother's, and hers before. I have never spent it. One day I shall, and it will buy something that cannot be bought twice. ...That was free. Do not grow used to it.

lines.speaker: vonnra

direction.notes: Matter-of-fact kindness. 'Somebody' might be someone long dead; don't lean on it.

lines.speaker: chid
lines.text: Can't sleep either?

context.where: over Chid's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to share a sleepless hour
direction.notes: A small warm aside, as if he has met many night-walkers like this.

lines.speaker: chid
lines.text: The dark's only the part of the day that hasn't happened yet. ...It's taking its time tonight.

context.where: over Chid's head as you pass, after dark

direction.pace: recited, then a slower wry aside
direction.wants: to hold on to the old words a little longer
direction.notes: The Order's saying comes out word-perfect from long use. Pause, then the aside about tonight is weary humour, not doubt.

lines.speaker: rav
lines.text: I'm a doctor. Don't make me prove it.

context.where: over Rav Cutwell's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to be left alone
direction.notes: Mock-threat with a grin under it.

lines.speaker: rav
lines.text: Red cloth's a hard habit to break.

context.where: over Rav Cutwell's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to belong somewhere
direction.notes: A half-sigh; the habit is his brother, unspoken.

lines.speaker: rav
lines.text: Buy me a drink and I'll tell you a lie worth hearing.

context.where: over Rav Cutwell's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to cadge a drink
direction.notes: Barroom hustle with a twinkle.

lines.speaker: rav
lines.text: Drop your trousers or don't. The leeches aren't fussy.

context.where: over Rav Cutwell's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to get on with the job
direction.notes: Doctor's frankness, completely unembarrassed; deadpan on the leeches.

lines.speaker: rav
lines.text: Half my patients die. The other half pay.

context.where: over Rav Cutwell's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to amuse himself
direction.notes: Grim joke, flat delivery, a ghost of a laugh.

lines.speaker: rav
lines.text: Pox, piles, a pike-wound or a broken heart: I've a cure for three of them and a drink for the fourth.

context.where: over Rav Cutwell's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to drum up custom
direction.notes: A tavern pitch with music in it; the broken heart gets a softer drink.

lines.speaker: rav
lines.text: Night surgery's double. Night anything's double.

context.where: over Rav Cutwell's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to joke about the late hour
direction.notes: Half-drunk drawl; the second sentence a leer, amused at himself.

lines.speaker: rav
lines.text: The best stories come after the third cup.

context.where: over Rav Cutwell's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to get the survivor to stay
direction.notes: Inviting; already past the third cup.

lines.speaker: rav
lines.text: Pull up a stool. Mind the blood.

context.where: over Rav Cutwell's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to welcome and unnerve
direction.notes: Warm invitation, then the blood line dry and unbothered.

lines.speaker: rav
lines.text: Last orders were an hour ago. I'm the only one who heard them.

context.where: over Rav Cutwell's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to keep drinking
direction.notes: Slurring a little; pleased with his own joke.

lines.speaker: harlan
lines.text: Late. Jory's never late.

context.where: over Harlan Coyle's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to reassure himself
direction.notes: Muttered; the second sentence a stubborn insistence that cracks a little on the name.

lines.speaker: harlan
lines.text: Salt, iron, cloth. Whatever you need, when the wagons come.

context.where: over Harlan Coyle's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to keep the stall going
direction.notes: A market cry with nothing behind it; 'when the wagons come' is the hope he is selling himself.

lines.speaker: harlan
lines.text: Somebody knows something.

context.where: over Harlan Coyle's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to find out who
direction.notes: Said to no one, a little resentful at the whole town.

lines.speaker: harlan
lines.text: I keep the books by candlelight. Helps me not think.

context.where: over Harlan Coyle's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to keep busy
direction.notes: Soft, tired, nearly confiding. 'Helps me not think' is a small honest admission.

lines.speaker: harlan
lines.text: Every wagon on that road's his, in the dark.

context.where: over Harlan Coyle's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to see Jory come home
direction.notes: Half a whisper, eyes on the dark road; the grief sounds almost like hope.

lines.speaker: harlan
lines.text: Can't sleep. Won't.

context.where: over Harlan Coyle's head as you pass, after dark

direction.pace: two clipped words, pause, one word
direction.wants: to stay awake for the boy
direction.notes: 'Won't' is a choice, firmer than 'Can't'.

lines.speaker: harlan
lines.text: Jory hated the dark. Hated it. Slept with a candle till he was fourteen.

context.where: over Harlan Coyle's head as you pass, after dark

direction.pace: repeat with a catch, then soft
direction.wants: to keep Jory near
direction.notes: The second 'Hated it' nearly a laugh; the candle detail is fond and hurts, because Jory is out in the dark.

lines.speaker: pell
lines.text: Everything has a price. Most things have two.

context.where: over Pell Varrow's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to amuse himself
direction.notes: Murmured, half a joke; smile on 'two'.

lines.speaker: pell
lines.text: Terrible business, Coyle's caravan. Terrible.

context.where: over Pell Varrow's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to be overheard sounding sorry
direction.notes: Practised condolence for the street; a trace of satisfaction under it.

lines.speaker: pell
lines.text: My warehouse is closed to the public.

context.where: over Pell Varrow's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to keep people out
direction.notes: A courteous notice spoken aloud; firmer than it needs to be.

lines.speaker: pell
lines.text: Closed. Closed! Come back in daylight.

context.where: over Pell Varrow's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to be left alone in the dark
direction.notes: The second 'Closed!' nearly loses control; 'Come back in daylight' is him reaching for manners.

lines.speaker: pell
lines.text: A man can't count in peace in this town.

context.where: over Pell Varrow's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to finish his sums
direction.notes: Grumbled to himself, fussy and tired.

lines.speaker: pell
lines.text: Who's there?

context.where: over Pell Varrow's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to know who is in the dark
direction.notes: Quick and a little high; he is frightened, so it is clipped and careful rather than loud.

lines.speaker: pell
lines.text: The numbers don't sleep. Why should I?

context.where: over Pell Varrow's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to keep counting
direction.notes: Tired and half-amused; the numbers he means are the ones in the hill.

lines.speaker: wenna
lines.text: The animals were never like this. Never.

context.where: over Old Wenna's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to be heard
direction.notes: Muttered to herself; the repeat 'Never' is stubborn and a bit scared, which she'd deny.

lines.speaker: wenna
lines.text: Bitterroot, bitterroot. Always need more.

context.where: over Old Wenna's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to remember her list
direction.notes: A grumbling refrain to herself as she sorts. Light.

lines.speaker: wenna
lines.text: The water tastes wrong this year.

context.where: over Old Wenna's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to know why
direction.notes: To herself, sniffing. A herbalist's worry, not a complaint.

lines.speaker: wenna
lines.text: Moon's up. Good for picking. Bad for knees.

context.where: over Old Wenna's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to get picking done
direction.notes: Old-woman humour; a grumble on 'knees'.

lines.speaker: wenna
lines.text: Mind the nettles in the dark.

context.where: over Old Wenna's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to stop someone getting stung
direction.notes: Said without looking. Rude-kind.

lines.speaker: wenna
lines.text: Night air's full of things. Some of them are herbs.

context.where: over Old Wenna's head as you pass, after dark

direction.pace: brisk, beat before the second half
direction.wants: to amuse herself
direction.notes: The pause makes the joke; slightly eerie, slightly wicked.

lines.speaker: wenna
lines.text: Nightshade's out. So are the idiots.

context.where: over Old Wenna's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to insult whoever's passing
direction.notes: Very rude, very pleased with herself. The jab lands on 'idiots'.

lines.speaker: tam
lines.text: They drank from the stream and fell down.

context.where: over Tam's head as you pass, day or night

direction.wants: to be believed
direction.notes: Said to anyone passing, the same fact again, a little louder each time.

lines.speaker: tam
lines.text: Pa says stay in town.

context.where: over Tam's head as you pass, day or night

direction.wants: to obey
direction.notes: Repeating Pa like a lesson; slightly bored.

lines.speaker: tam
lines.text: I told the Watch. The Watch laughed.

context.where: over Tam's head as you pass, day or night

direction.wants: to be taken seriously
direction.notes: 'The Watch laughed' is a child's grievance; flat with hurt, never sarcastic.

lines.speaker: brannoc
lines.text: Good steel's not cheap. Nor's a good pelt.

context.where: over Brannoc's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to set a fair price
direction.notes: A trade maxim over the anvil; a little dry. Balance the two halves like scales.

lines.speaker: brannoc
lines.text: Mind the sparks.

context.where: over Brannoc's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to keep a passer-by unburnt
direction.notes: Barely looks up; a warning that's also mild care. Two words, no lift.

lines.speaker: brannoc
lines.text: Bring me hides. I'll make you something worth wearing.

context.where: over Brannoc's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to get hides
direction.notes: The nearest he comes to selling. Plain, a hint of pride on 'worth wearing'.

lines.speaker: brannoc
lines.text: Hit a man with this and he stays hit.

context.where: over Brannoc's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to show off the weight of good iron
direction.notes: A dry joke he doesn't smile at. Lean on 'stays hit' like the hammer landing.

lines.speaker: brannoc
lines.text: Forge is banked. First light.

context.where: over Brannoc's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to say come back later
direction.notes: Not unkind; just the hour. Low and drowsy.

lines.speaker: brannoc
lines.text: Arm aches worse at night. Old iron does.

context.where: over Brannoc's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to name the ache
direction.notes: Talking about his arm the way others talk about weather; 'old iron' is him. A low, private grumble.

lines.speaker: brannoc
lines.text: Fire keeps me company.

context.where: over Brannoc's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to not be alone
direction.notes: The fire is all he has with Nell gone; he doesn't know he's saying it. Quiet, almost tender; no self-pity.

lines.speaker: brannoc
lines.text: Banked. Go away.

context.where: over Brannoc's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to be left alone
direction.notes: Blunt, not hostile. Two strokes.

lines.speaker: brannoc
lines.text: Two on the rack. Leave them.

context.where: over Brannoc's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to keep the last two irons from anyone
direction.notes: He's watching the rack at night for the buyer. Quiet threat in a tired voice; firm on 'Leave them'.

lines.speaker: vonnra
lines.text: The toll is the toll.

context.where: over Vonnra Ash-of-Morrow's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to restate the terms to whoever passes
direction.notes: Said to the air, as a rule of nature.

lines.speaker: vonnra
lines.text: I see a great deal. I say very little. You will find that is the arrangement.

context.where: over Vonnra Ash-of-Morrow's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to keep strangers at their proper distance
direction.notes: A recited creed. Faint amusement at the predictability of those who will ask anyway.

lines.speaker: vonnra
lines.text: Payment, always.

context.where: over Vonnra Ash-of-Morrow's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to keep the arrangement in everyone's ears
direction.notes: Neither greedy nor warm; the way a clock says the hour.

lines.speaker: vonnra
lines.text: The toll does not sleep, and neither do I.

context.where: over Vonnra Ash-of-Morrow's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to show she is always keeping watch
direction.notes: She does not sleep because she is waiting on the ford. Plain statement, a breath of weariness underneath.

lines.speaker: vonnra
lines.text: The dark is also a customer.

context.where: over Vonnra Ash-of-Morrow's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to remind herself what the night buys
direction.notes: Bone-dry; she has done business with the dark and knows it.

lines.speaker: vonnra
lines.text: Payment, even now.

context.where: over Vonnra Ash-of-Morrow's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to keep the terms whatever the hour
direction.notes: Low and steady. The 'even now' is tired and unyielding.

lines.speaker: vonnra
lines.text: The ford is quiet tonight. It will not stay quiet.

context.where: over Vonnra Ash-of-Morrow's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to keep watch on what she set going
direction.notes: She is looking south toward the crossing. The second sentence is certainty, not fear.

lines.speaker: keegan
lines.text: None pass north. Not yet.

context.where: over Dame Keegan Orme's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to hold the gate
direction.notes: Clear command, with a hopeful lift on 'Not yet'.

lines.speaker: keegan
lines.text: You are not ready for what is beyond there.

context.where: over Dame Keegan Orme's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to warn passers-by off
direction.notes: Lecturer's gravity; she believes it and is a little proud of the phrasing.

lines.speaker: keegan
lines.text: Probationary. It is a real title.

context.where: over Dame Keegan Orme's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to insist on her standing
direction.notes: Rehearsed retort, said to nobody, as if continuing an argument from earlier.

lines.speaker: keegan
lines.text: Night watch. Probationary night watch.

context.where: over Dame Keegan Orme's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to remind herself why she is still awake
direction.notes: Flat comic correction on 'Probationary'.

lines.speaker: keegan
lines.text: Something moved out there. Probably.

context.where: over Dame Keegan Orme's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to reassure herself
direction.notes: Alert, then deflating into a doubtful 'Probably'. A little jumpier than she would admit.

lines.speaker: keegan
lines.text: Stand back from the gate, please.

context.where: over Dame Keegan Orme's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to keep the gate clear
direction.notes: Correct and civil; the 'please' is policy, not nerves.

lines.speaker: keegan
lines.text: I am not frightened of the dark. I am merely monitoring it very closely.

context.where: over Dame Keegan Orme's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to convince herself she is not afraid
direction.notes: Pompous diction covering real fear of the dark. 'Very closely' gets a nervous emphasis.

lines.speaker: sella
lines.text: Buy a girl a drink? No? Buy yourself one, then. You look like you need it.

context.where: over Sella's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to start a conversation
direction.notes: Cheerful hustle; the second half is friendly, not hurt.

lines.speaker: sella
lines.text: You've got road on you. I can smell it from here.

context.where: over Sella's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to catch the passer's eye
direction.notes: Amused, nose-wrinkling, warm.

lines.speaker: sella
lines.text: Rook's stew or my company. Only one of them's warm.

context.where: over Sella's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to tempt
direction.notes: Low, dry; a smile on 'warm'.

lines.speaker: sella
lines.text: Cold night to sleep alone, love.

context.where: over Sella's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to fill the blue room
direction.notes: Plain and warm, a working line; not breathy.

lines.speaker: sella
lines.text: Rook's walls are thin. Just so you know.

context.where: over Sella's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to warn and tease
direction.notes: A friendly tip; the amusement is in what she leaves out.

lines.speaker: sella
lines.text: The blue room's got a lamp lit. Guess who's in it.

context.where: over Sella's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to advertise
direction.notes: Bright and knowing; she enjoys her own sign.

lines.speaker: sella
lines.text: Rook's walls are thin and I'm not quiet. Fair warning.

context.where: over Sella's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to joke with the passer
direction.notes: Unembarrassed, funny; 'Fair warning' dead dry.

lines.speaker: redcowl
lines.text: Keep walking.

context.where: over Redcowl's head as you pass, day or night

direction.wants: to be left alone
direction.notes: Two words, flat, not shouted.

lines.speaker: redcowl
lines.text: Salvage is salvage.

context.where: over Redcowl's head as you pass, day or night

direction.wants: to justify his trade
direction.notes: Matter-of-fact; a creed, not an excuse.

lines.speaker: redcowl
lines.text: Talk or bleed. Your choice.

context.where: over Redcowl's head as you pass, day or night

direction.wants: to remind everyone who's in charge
direction.notes: Almost cheerful, then 'Your choice' drops cold.

lines.speaker: redcowl
lines.text: Last man who lied to me, I nailed his tongue to a cart and let the horse decide.

context.where: over Redcowl's head as you pass, day or night

direction.wants: to make a story of a threat
direction.notes: Told like a joke with a chuckle at 'let the horse decide'; under it, nobody is sure it isn't true.

lines.speaker: jory
lines.text: I thought I'd die in that cage.

context.where: over Jory Coyle's head as you pass, day or night

direction.wants: to say it out loud and be rid of it
direction.notes: Muttered, not for anyone; matter-of-fact on the surface, a shiver under it.

lines.speaker: jory
lines.text: Uncle keeps hugging me. It's a lot.

context.where: over Jory Coyle's head as you pass, day or night

direction.wants: to be allowed some space
direction.notes: Seventeen and mortified, but he doesn't mind really; 'It's a lot' is fond.

lines.speaker: jory
lines.text: There was a fourth cage. Was.

context.where: over Jory Coyle's head as you pass, day or night

direction.pace: flat statement, then a stark single word
direction.wants: to not have seen what he saw
direction.notes: 'Was.' is the whole line: someone in it died. Pause before it; say it flat and quiet.

lines.speaker: wayfinder
lines.text: Maps! Places the road forgets. Some of them it forgot on purpose.

context.where: over Ysolde Marrow's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to draw in customers
direction.notes: Market-stall call; a darker, quieter twist on 'on purpose'.

lines.speaker: wayfinder
lines.text: Every map on this table was drawn by someone who came back. Not always all of them.

context.where: over Ysolde Marrow's head as you pass, by day

direction.pace: brisk, a pause before 'Not always all of them'
direction.wants: to sell the maps truthfully
direction.notes: Gallows humour delivered as a selling point.

lines.speaker: wayfinder
lines.text: Read the oaths in the margins before you go. They are not decoration.

context.where: over Ysolde Marrow's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to make sure buyers read the fine print
direction.notes: A pedant's insistence; 'not decoration' a little sharp.

lines.speaker: wayfinder
lines.text: Half an hour in there and the thing that owns it comes to see who's making the noise.

context.where: over Ysolde Marrow's head as you pass, by day

direction.wants: to tell the half-hour rule as a warning
direction.notes: Said lightly, like weather. The 'thing' is spoken of with familiarity, not dread.

lines.speaker: wayfinder
lines.text: The ink is still wet on this one. So is the blood.

context.where: over Ysolde Marrow's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to unsettle and intrigue passers-by
direction.notes: Quiet aside. The blood line is plain fact with a dry smile behind it.

lines.speaker: wayfinder
lines.text: Night maps cost the same. They just feel dearer.

context.where: over Ysolde Marrow's head as you pass, after dark

direction.wants: to make light of the late hour
direction.notes: Night trade; a small, weary joke.

lines.text: A Watchman, grey-bearded and a long time dead, sitting against the post as if he had only stopped for breath. Something has had his eyes.
